text:
emily_cs: customer reported rerank returning all zero/identical scores for a set of inputs, 422 on some payloads. believe it's an input-shape issue but can't repro locally. attaching minimal payload they used.

emily_cs: payload (redacted):
```json
{
  "query": { "text": "what is the refund policy" },
  "documents": [
    { "id": "d1", "metadata": {"source":"kb"}, "passages": [{"text": "Refunds processed within 30 days"}] },
    { "id": "d2", "passages": [{"text": "No refunds after 30 days"}] }
  ]
}
```

emily_cs: they said when they move the same query object to root as a string (query: "..."), scores behave normally.

jordan_support: can you paste the exact error response for the 422?

emily_cs: "422 Unprocessable Entity: ambiguous field 'query' found in document payload (docs vs root)". also a case where API returns 200 but all scores == 0.0 for some variations.

sanjay_eng: thanks. initial hunch: our rerank schema expects a root-level query string or a specific queryKey tied to candidates. nesting query as an object inside root but colliding with docs[].metadata.query could confuse the parser. can you share a minimal curl we can run?

jordan_support: i reproduced quickly by sending the payload above to staging-rerank. behavior: 422 when documents contain a top-level "query" key inside metadata or passages, 200+zero scores when query is present but candidate text path resolves to empty strings (we had a bug where passages[] was prioritized over candidate text).

jordan_support: quick repro curl we used: 
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"query":"what is the refund policy","candidates":[{"id":"c1","text":"Refunds processed within 30 days"},{"id":"c2","text":"No refunds after 30 days"}] }'
```

jordan_support: that one returns non-zero scores. the failing payloads either used "documents" with nested "passages" or put "query" as an object which we don't map by default.

qa-bot: automated test run: rerank/nested-query-leak -> fail. stack trace points to parseCandidates() trying to flatten docs -> uses key precedence: candidates > documents > docs[].passages. if docs has a key named "query" we accidentally overwrite the request-level query variable.

sanjay_eng: confirmed. root cause: field shadowing during request normalization. workaround: flatten to use explicit "candidates" array with text fields, or rename embedded fields in docs (avoid top-level key "query" inside docs metadata). long term: patch parser to namespace doc keys and prefer explicit request.query. I'll open an eng ticket and a tiny staging patch to fail-fast on ambiguous keys.

emily_cs: can you put the workaround steps in a short snippet I can send to the customer?

sanjay_eng: copy-paste this workaround for now:
```
// Option A: use candidates explicitly
{
  "query": "what is the refund policy",
  "candidates": [
    {"id":"c1","text":"Refunds processed within 30 days"},
    {"id":"c2","text":"No refunds after 30 days"}
  ]
}
// Option B: if sending documents with passages, ensure you DO NOT include a key named "query" inside documents or passages metadata
```

sanjay_eng: i created ENG-1427 to fix normalization + added a validation error for ambiguous keys. staging patch scheduled in 30m.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: rerank-parser-fix -> staging at 2026-03-17T15:40Z (rolling).

emily_cs: thanks all. i'll send workaround + ETA to the customer and flag for priority if they can't change payload shape. if staging patch works we can offer to route them to staging temporary. :thumbsup:
